name: Kalmegh
actions: Traditionally used for fevers and the liver
traditionalUses: Sluggish digestion and liver in tradition
kitchenUse: Not a kitchen herb; extremely bitter, taken as powder, decoction or tablets.

typicalUse.adultAmount: Only as a qualified practitioner advises; products and strengths vary

cautions.note: Avoid in pregnancy; it may cause miscarriage. Also avoid while breastfeeding.
Serious allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported.
It may stimulate the immune system; avoid with autoimmune conditions.
May slow blood clotting; stop two weeks before surgery.

interactions.effect: May add to the effect of blood thinners.

evidence.summary: Several trials suggest andrographis may ease cold and sore throat symptoms, but many were small or of uncertain quality.
